purpose: This medicine replaces the digestive enzymes that your pancreas is not making enough of on its own. It helps your body properly break down and absorb fats, proteins, and carbohydrates from the food you eat. It is commonly used for conditions like cystic fibrosis, chronic pancreatitis, or after pancreatic surgery.
how_it_works: Your pancreas normally makes special proteins called enzymes that help digest your food. When your pancreas is not working well, you do not have enough of these enzymes, so food does not get digested or absorbed properly. This medication gives your body those missing enzymes — lipase to digest fats, protease to digest proteins, and amylase to digest carbohydrates — so your body can get the nutrition it needs.
common_side_effects: Stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation are the most common side effects. Some people may notice greasy or unusual stools, especially when the dose is being adjusted. Headache and dizziness can also occur.
warnings: Do not switch between brands without talking to your doctor or pharmacist, since different brands are not interchangeable. Taking very high doses can rarely cause a serious bowel condition, so always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Tell your doctor if you are allergic to pork products, since this medication is made from pork pancreas. Do not crush or chew the capsules or the beads inside — swallow them whole or mix the beads with soft acidic food like applesauce.
typical_dosing: The dose is individualized for each person based on your condition, weight, and the amount of fat in your diet. Capsules are taken with every meal and snack — usually half the meal dose is taken with snacks. Always take it with food or drinks (never on an empty stomach) and follow your doctor's specific instructions exactly.
